title: Escalation quickplay: canary response scripts and communication ladder
collaborators: Liam O'Connor; Priya Singh; Marco Alvarez
content:
Summary: This quickplay is a lightweight, cross-functional runbook for responding to canaries and small A/B exposures. It prioritizes fast containment, clear ownership, and minimal disruption to stable traffic. Use this when a monitoring alert or stakeholder call indicates unexpected behavior during an exposure ramp.

Audience: release leads, on-call SREs, product managers, console engineers, solutions engineers, customer-facing support.

Primary objectives:
- Contain user impact within minutes.
- Restore baseline traffic routing ASAP.
- Preserve forensic data for post-incident analysis.

Minimal checks before action (0-3 min):
1) Verify signal provenance: which dashboard/alert fired, time window, cohort id, route, model variant, exposure pct.
2) Confirm whether baseline (control) looks unchanged. If the control cohort is also degraded, treat as infra incident.
3) If noisy/uncertain signal, run synthetic prompts (mini-eval) against both variants while proceeding with safe containment.

Containment patterns (pick one based on signal):
- Latency-only spike: cut exposure to 25% of current or route to lighter-weight variant. Watch p95 for 5m.
- Error spike (4xx/5xx): immediate rollback to previous deploy for model-serving infra changes; otherwise reduce exposure to 0-1% and quarantine requests.
- Quality regression (automated eval or customer report): pause expansion, stop ramp, and divert traffic to control cohort. If harmful content, hard-stop exposure to 0%.
- Cost anomaly: disable nonessential caching and reduce exposure by 50% and page finance-on-call.

Rapid actions (console-first recommended):
- Pause exposure (console): click route -> pause rollout -> reason "pause: signal breach"
- Set exposure to X% (CLI shorthand): redwood set-exposure --route <route> --cohort <cohort> --percent <X> --reason "canary containment"
- Swap variant: redwood set-route-variant --route <route> --variant <variant-id> --force --audit-note "rollback-canary"
- Snapshot telemetry: redwood snapshot --route <route> --window 15m --tag canary-investigation --dest s3://redwood-artifacts/canary-snaps/<iso>.json

Decision ladder (who to call and when):
- Triage (0-10m): on-call SRE + release lead. Perform containment action and post initial note in #canary-triage.
- Contain (10-30m): product PM + console engineer + solutions eng. If containment fails or user-impact suspected, open war room.
- War room (30-90m): serving runtime lead, SRE manager, product lead, CS lead. Coordinate customer comms and remediation.
- Exec notify (>90m or critical customer impact): CTO, Head of Product, Legal.

Communication snippets (copy/paste):
- Slack triage post:
  [CANARY] route=<route>, variant=<variant>, exposure=<pct> — observed: p95 latency +350ms vs baseline; action: reduced exposure to 10% and snapshotting. Owner: @oncall-sre. Dashboards: <link>.

- War room invite (brief):
  War room: canary failure — route=<route>. Timeline: deploy -> ramp -> detection. Immediate asks: trace replay, rollback option, customer-impact check. Join: <zoom>.

Fast diagnostics checklist (first 15m):
- Compare p50/p95 by variant and control, error codes breakdown, region distribution, recent infra deploys, GPU/host metrics (GPU mem, GPU utilization), request size distribution, caching hit rates, mini-eval failures.

Guiding heuristics (operational):
- Prefer routing change over code rollback when experiments are isolated routing flags.
- Prefer quick exposure reductions over multiple toggles: one clear change with observation window.
- Favor console UI when audit trail matters (post-incident compliance).

Example scenarios (to illustrate):
1) Small latency bump (p95 +220ms) after a variant swap: reduce exposure to 25%, observe 10m; if stable, incrementally restore or continue roll forward after investigation.
2) Sudden error surge 10m after ramp with 5xx spikes localized to a region: isolate region routing, reduce exposure globally to 1%, escalate to SRE infra.
3) A/B shows -3% primary metric (stat sig) but no safety flags: stop ramp, trigger human review of 50 failed prompts, collect for model team.

Post-incident deliverables (within 48h):
- Incident doc: timeline with exact exposure changes, log slices, hypothesis, fix, and owner for each follow-up. Attach telemetry snapshot and mini-eval outputs.
- Experiment manifest updates: adjust thresholds, required dashboards, and roll-forward criteria.
- Alert tuning: reduce noisy signals, add guardrails for safety-classifier thresholds.

Short pager response templates (single-line):
- ACK & contain: "Acknowledged. Reducing exposure to 10% and snapshotting metrics. Will update in 5m. --@oncall-sre"
- Escalate to war room: "Containment unsuccessful; opening war room now. Hypothesis: model variant-induced latency. CC: product + serving runtime. --@release-lead"

Open items / action list:
- Integrate auto-mini-eval into canary pipelines (infra PR pending). Owner: Marco. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Add mandatory alert links into experiment manifest so triage knows which dashboard to open. Owner: Priya. ETA: 1 week.
- Prototype Slack quick-actions for exposure changes with audit metadata. Owner: Liam. ETA: 3 weeks.

Notes (informal):
- Keep this doc intentionally narrow: link to full incident playbooks for infra or security incidents.
- Encourage teams to set experiment-specific thresholds; this quickplay should not override experiment owners' guardrails.
